relevance: Same design question as your source-conditioned models: what to put at t = 0. A gene-level prediction (as in scIso) could serve as the source, with the flow learning only the isoform-level residual.
summary: For combinatorial perturbations, most of the response is the sum of single-perturbation effects. SynGeneFlow anchors the flow's source distribution at that additive prior and learns only the residual flow to the true perturbed state.
takeaways: Choosing an informative source distribution focuses model capacity on the hard, non-additive part of the signal.
Gene-gene interactions enter as a static mask plus a perturbation-dependent bias in the network.
MMD regularisation on both the endpoint and the residual distributions keeps population-level structure.
title: Synergy-Aware Residual Flow Matching for Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction (SynGeneFlow)

relevance: The current argument for continuous flows over discrete diffusion on discrete data. Useful context for your choice between a CTMC on the lattice simplex and continuous simplex flows, and it connects to the flow-map papers already on your path.
summary: A continuous flow language model scaled to 8B parameters by adapting a pretrained autoregressive model: causal attention over the prefix and bidirectional, asynchronous flow within each block. Trained on fewer than 30B tokens.
takeaways: Matches or beats the autoregressive base on instruction following, reasoning and coding, and can be distilled into flow maps for one- or few-step generation.
Flow training acts like multi-token prediction and can even improve the AR capabilities it starts from.
A self-speculative decoding scheme (flow drafts, AR verification in one model) gives about 2.5x AR throughput and beats discrete diffusion at comparable quality.
title: Large Flow Language Models (Lafa)

relevance: A cheap upgrade to try in your hierarchical NB + multinomial VAE baseline: swap the standard normal prior for this one and compare ELBOs and cell-type clustering. David Knowles also works on splicing (LeafCutter), so his group may follow up on isoform-level models.
summary: Revisits the VampPrior, which approximates the optimal VAE prior (the aggregate posterior) with a mixture of encoder outputs at learned pseudo-inputs. It fixes two weaknesses: prior and posterior share one amortised covariance, and the mixture weights are fixed and uniform.
takeaways: Decoupling the prior and posterior covariances removes a conflict between wanting high-entropy priors and low-entropy posteriors, and raises model evidence.
Replacing the uniform mixture with a Dirichlet process gives non-parametric clustering in latent space.
Dropping the new prior into scVI improves integration and clustering across six single-cell atlases. Only the prior changes, so it works with any continuous-latent DLVM.
title: VampPrior Unleashed
